Meanwhile, Nvidia and Anthropic surged as artificial intelligence-linked stocks tried to recover after last week's sharp declines. Follow below as CNBC highlights the biggest stock moves of the day. 15 Min Ago General Motors moves higher after report on Barra successor Shares of General Motors added more than 2% following a Bloomberg report that said executive Sterling Anderson is being considered as a potential successor to CEO Mary Barra. The company's board wants the next leader to have an expertise in software and self-driving technology, Bloomberg said, citing people familiar with the board's thinking. Anderson came to GM in June 2025, leaving behind the self-driving vehicle technology startup he co-founded, Aurora Innovation. Prior to that he was the director of autopilot programs at Tesla. — Michelle Fox 34 Min Ago Dollar General rises on upgrade Shares of Dollar General moved 2% higher on the back of an upgrade to overweight from neutral at Piper Sandler. Analyst Peter Keith said comparable sales growth and margin expansion should help the discount retailer reach a high-teens earnings-per-share compound annual growth rate over the next three years. Plus, the company's steady growth profile is appealing in an increasingly volatile market environment, he said. — Michelle Fox 58 Min Ago LuxExperience pops after JPMorgan upgrade JPMorgan upgraded the luxury digital retailer to overweight from neutral on Monday, sending U.S.-listed shares up 6.6% in premarket trading. The bank, which recently hosted a fireside chat with LuxExperience CEO Michael Klinger at a Paris conference, said the company is favorably positioned at the intersection of luxury and e-commerce. It is "notably emerging as the last man standing within an increasingly fragmented and consolidating competitive landscape, with $1B+ of market share opportunity, in our view, over the next 12-24 months across the portfolio," analyst Matthew Boss said in a note Monday. — Michelle Fox 59 Min Ago Mara, Strategy jump as crypto rebounds Shares of Mara Holdings and Strategy popped 7.6% and 8.5%, respectively, as bitcoin tried to recover some of the steep losses suffered last week. Bitcoin was last up 1.1% at $61,291.08. The flagship cryptocurrency last week traded below $60,000 for the first time since July. MARA 5-day chart — Fred Imbert 2 Hours Ago Citizens, Truist rise after Baird upgrades Citizens and Truist gained more than 2% each after the regional banks were upgraded by Baird to outperform from neutral. Analyst David George highlighted Citizens's attractive valuation at about 1.7 times price to book value. "CFG has a clear path to NIM expansion through 2027, which should drive healthy NII growth even if the operating environment worsens. A growing Private Bank contribution and improving operating leverage add to that momentum and create an attractive risk/reward trade-off," he said. Regarding Truist, he said the stock's valuation mitigates downside risk, along with moves made by management. "We believe recent weakness in the banks provides us the opportunity to buy TFC, as new CEO Mike Lyons will make incremental progress improving the returns and EPS power over time. We expect Lyons and his team to improve the economics of its balance sheet while self-funding growth initiatives to jump-start revenue growth longer term." — Fred Imbert 2 Hours Ago Nvidia, Anthropic surge in early trading Shares of Nvidia and Anthropic popped 8% and 4%, respectively, as investors scooped up AI-linked names at a discount after a steep sell-off last week . headlines.article_text: SpaceX sued by 2 states over AI deepfake porn, Grok safety claims Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Virginia and Oregon are the first states to sue Elon Musk's SpaceX, alleging it harmed consumers and falsely marketed its Grok AI image generator as generally safe. Grok, which is integrated with social network X, has enabled users to generate and share explicit deepfakes based on real images of children and women who did not consent, research shows. The states' attorneys general are seeking civil penalties, fees and to make SpaceX put stricter guardrails in place. In this article SPCX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Jonathan Raa | Nurphoto | Getty Images Lawsuits against Elon Musk's SpaceX are stacking up, with Virginia and Oregon becoming the first states to sue the company over issues with its Grok AI image generator. Versions of Grok and SpaceX's social network X have enabled users to generate and distribute explicit deepfakes based on real photos or videos of children and other people who did not consent, according to research by the Internet Watch Foundation , the Center for Countering Digital Hate and others. In separate complaints submitted to state courts as of Monday morning, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones argued that SpaceX failed to put safeguards in place to stop Grok and X users from making and sharing harmful deepfake images, especially alleged AI-generated child sexual abuse material. The complaints also allege that SpaceX has falsely represented its AI apps and social network (Grok and X) as generally safe, which the states see as a violation of Virginia's Consumer Protection Act or Oregon's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. The matter is particularly concerning because X allows minors 13 and older to access its content. Rayfield and Jones both noted in their complaints that harms caused by non-consensual, sexualized images go beyond the victims depicted in the images. "This content can cause fear, distress, and anxiety in those who are unwillingly exposed to the content," Jones wrote. Rayfield wrote that such conduct "erodes important norms regarding consent and privacy and trivializes sexual imagery, abuse, and exploitation." SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment. headlines.article_text: Tokenized stocks face pushback as NYSE, Nasdaq pivot for a new market Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points People involved in talks with some of the companies say a 30-day objection window left them little time to react and decide if they were ready to participate. In this article ICE Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, Nov. 10, 2026. Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images OKXICE, a trading platform for tokenized securities jointly operated by Intercontinental Exchange and crypto exchange OKX, is set to debut Monday despite objections from 90% of the companies whose stocks it initially proposed to list. Of the 62 companies whose shares OKICE first sought to trade, 56 objected to having their shares tokenized and traded on the platform, according to a review of public notices posted between Oct. 4 and Nov. 5 . By last week, even more companies had objected , including those not on the original roster. The high objection rate may reflect companies' lack of readiness to have blockchain-based representations of their shares traded on a new third-party platform like OKXICE, rather than broad resistance to tokenization. People involved in talks with some of the companies say a 30-day objection window left them little time to react and decide if they were ready to participate. `Revolutionary,' 'transformational' "The shift to a 24/7 global marketplace is revolutionary and transformational for our market structure," Andrew Cuomo, co-chair of OKXICE, told CNBC. "The majority of companies aren't familiar with [tokenization] and haven't had a chance to understand it and the consequences." "Logic dictates that many companies were going to be cautious before they understood what the system would do," added Cuomo, who served 10 years as governor of New York until 2021. "What you're seeing now is the more the companies learn about 24/7 global access, the more receptive they are." At launch, tokenized shares of Coinbase , Robinhood , Strategy , Circle , Securitize and BitGo will be available to trade on the platform, OKXICE disclosed in a public notice. OKXICE has confirmed 113 assets, including exchange-traded funds and products, going live on a rolling basis. Since its initial pre-launch announcement on Nov. 11, OKXICE said it's seen further interest from different issuers and Fidelity Investments , Direxion, eToro , Strive and Vida Global are now participating. The 30-day opt-out window is a requirement of the SEC's so-called Innovation Exemption , which took effect in September and temporarily permits the trading of certain tokenized stocks. Under the exemption, trading platforms must notify the underlying issuers and give them an opportunity to object. Any issuer who objects blocks its shares from being tokenized. "We've gotten a lot of feedback that the reason why you've seen this high number of rejections of tokenizing equity is because it was a 30-day window," Seth Ginns, chief investment officer at Franklin Templeton's crypto arm, told CNBC at the Digital Assets Forum in New York earlier this month. Many issuers were open to exploring the idea but were hesitant to move forward amid competing priorities, he said. "[They're] saying it's earnings season, there was the midterms, there's a lot going on during this 30-day window. Give us some time, we want to learn about it, we're not closed to the idea we're just closed to rushing into it right now," Ginns added. Announcement timing Ran Grushkowsky, CEO of MassPay, a global payout platform, said several of his company's clients were among the initial targets and shared that their concern was less about the concept of tokenization and more about how 24/7 trading could affect stock value and investor relations strategies, particularly around the timing of corporate announcements. "It's more [about] what's going to be the effect, how is it going to actually drive the value of the stock," he said. "A lot of the strategy that happens around investors relations has to do with scheduling and when you announce certain things and so how do you do it when your stock is being traded 24/7?" watch now VIDEO 9:59 09:59 Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo on scaling tokenization and expanding beyond digital securities Crypto "The executives were actually quite excited about this new innovation and potentially getting more interest into the stock. It was really from the [investor relations] side that they received push back," and heard "let's hold off," Grushkowsky added. The lack of awareness may even extend to executives overseeing digital asset initiatives, suggesting that some rejections stem from internal communication gaps and unfamiliarity with the process, according to Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo, whose company is one of the first being listed on OKX. Securitize is also the tokenization partner for OKX. "We've talked to some of the issuers that have opted out [where] the head of digital assets doesn't even know who in the company rejected them," he said. "This is a consequence of, first, the novelty of the process and of these venues, and second, the lack of understanding of what they're being notified to do." watch now VIDEO 3:05 03:05 Robinhood CEO on tokenization: It allows us to distribute access to U.S. stocks globally Squawk Box Despite the initial pushback, Domingo expects more issuers to participate as companies become more familiar with the model, noting that some regulated trading venues can operate without issuer consent. Long game Company objections raise a separate question about which of the different tokenization models will prove most attractive. The main alternative to the OKXICE model is an issuer-led approach that integrates blockchain-based shares into existing regulated market infrastructures, with issuers retaining greater control over the process.
